h1: Humz Canal Stay — A 70-Year-Old Wooden House on Om Non Canal, Now Four Water-View Rooms for Anyone Wanting to Escape the City
intro: If you want to fall asleep to the sound of water and wake up to sunrise over a canal — without driving out of the city — Humz Canal Stay is a tiny place renovated from a 70-year-old wooden house on the Om Non Canal in Bang Kruai, Mueang Nonthaburi, just on the edge of Bangkok · It has only 4 rooms — 1 Canal Suite and 3 Canal Deluxe — and every one has a timber terrace projecting over the water where you can sip coffee and watch the boats go by all day · Guests consistently praise the peaceful atmosphere, the warm hosts who look after you like family, and the pinto-style Thai breakfast · The trade-offs are a fairly tucked-away location that's hard to reach by ride-hailing, firm mattresses, and some boat or community noise at night · Rooms start from approx. ฿2,300/night.

body.html: Humz Canal Stay isn't a hotel in the usual sense — it's a 70-year-old wooden house that the owners renovated into a canal-side stay on the Om Non Canal in Bang Krang, Mueang Nonthaburi · The old timber frame and the posts planted in the water are still there; comfort has been added the way a hotel would, without cutting the place off from the riverside way of life of the Bang Kruai community · There are just 4 rooms in total — 1 Canal Suite, the largest, and 3 Canal Deluxe rooms · Every room has a timber terrace projecting out over the canal; open the folding doors and the water fills your view, with long-tail boats passing, wooden houses on both banks, and the sun slipping below the water in the evening.

The rooms are designed to sleep comfortably like a hotel, with air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a desk, and an en-suite bathroom finished in plain white tile that looks clean and simple · What guests mention most is how peaceful it is — quiet enough that you feel a world away from the city; sitting on the terrace in the morning with a coffee, listening to the water lap against the posts, is the moment many say made the trip worth it · But there are honest caveats to know before booking: the mattresses are fairly thin and firm, with some reviews calling them around 10 cm thick, so anyone who likes a soft bed may need to adjust, and small items such as soap, a mosquito net or a few utensils aren't always provided as fully as at a large hotel — bring your essentials with you.

"The canal-view room is beautiful — open the terrace and the water is right there, and it's so peaceful. The owner and staff are lovely and look after you like family · breakfast came in a pinto and was both adorable and delicious — perfect for couples wanting to escape the chaos."

What gives Humz Canal Stay more charm than an ordinary stay are the activities and spots tied to the water · On site there's a riverside café called The Canal Club for relaxing among the greenery, and you can take a kayak out and explore the Om Non Canal yourself — an old waterway still full of riverside life, temples and orchards to paddle past · Breakfast is served pinto-style (a Thai tiffin carrier) and many reviews praise it as tasty and prettily presented, with staff happy to serve it early for guests rushing to a flight · Note that this is a small stay with no swimming pool, gym or hotel-style lobby, and it accepts adults aged 18 and over only, with no extra beds, so it suits couples or anyone wanting privacy more than families with young children.

Be clear about the location before booking · The stay sits down a quiet lane on the canal in Bang Kruai, around 9 km from central Nonthaburi and roughly 20–28 km from central Bangkok · The upside is real peace and privacy, but the trade-off many reviews flag is that getting a Grab or taxi in and out is tricky because it's tucked away and Google Maps directions can sometimes lead you astray · Driving yourself is easiest, with free parking on site · It's about 11 km from Don Mueang Airport, while the MRT Purple and Red lines are a connecting ride away · The overall score sits around 9.0 from roughly 48 real guest reviews, which is high for a small, atmosphere-led stay.

Honestly, Humz Canal Stay is a place for travellers chasing atmosphere and quiet rather than full convenience · If you're a couple, a worker wanting to escape the city and breathe, or someone who loves photographing riverside life, sleeping in an old wooden house over a quiet canal for around ฿2,300 is an experience you won't find in a high-rise hotel · But if you want a soft bed, full facilities, easy transport with quick ride-hailing, or you're mainly here to see Bangkok, a stay by the MRT or in the city will suit you far better · This is a place to choose only if it matches what you actually want.

A tip from following the reviews here: book well in advance, because with only 4 rooms it fills up fast, especially on weekends · Before you travel, get the exact pin or the owner's contact, since Google Maps can mislead and ride-hailing is hard to catch out here — driving yourself is the most relaxing option · If you're a light sleeper, the firm mattresses or boat noise mean a favourite pillow or earplugs are worth packing · Bring personal items like soap, your own medication and mosquito repellent · And don't miss waking early to watch the sunrise over the canal from your terrace and taking a kayak out — that's the heart of staying here.

honestSummary: Humz Canal Stay is a place that puts atmosphere and quiet first — ideal for couples or anyone wanting to escape the city and sleep to the sound of water on the Om Non Canal · The renovated 70-year-old wooden house, a water-view terrace in every room, kayaking and a pinto breakfast are genuine charms — but you have to accept fairly firm mattresses, just 4 rooms that are hard to book, a tucked-away location that's hard to reach by ride-hailing, and an adults-only policy that doesn't suit families with young children.
honestChecks: If you want a soft bed, full facilities and easy transport with quick ride-hailing — the mattresses here are firm and it's down a quiet lane → a hotel in central Nonthaburi or by the MRT Purple Line will be more convenient.

If you're travelling as a family with young children, or want a swimming pool — Humz is adults-only (18+), with no extra beds and no pool → a riverside resort like Kalanan Riverside Resort in Pak Kret suits families better.

If your main goal is sightseeing or business in central Bangkok — this sits down a canal lane in Bang Kruai and needs a connecting ride into the city → a hotel in Bangkok or by the MRT will save far more time.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Humz Canal Stay, Nonthaburi

faq.q: Where is Humz Canal Stay, and is it easy to reach?
faq.a: It's at 66 Moo 6, Bang Kruai-Sai Noi Road, Bang Krang, Mueang Nonthaburi, on the Om Non Canal in Bang Kruai · The upside is real peace and privacy, but it's down a quiet lane — catching a Grab or taxi in and out is tricky and Google Maps can mislead, so get the owner's pin before you go. Driving yourself is easiest, with free parking · It's about 9 km from central Nonthaburi, 11 km from Don Mueang Airport, and roughly 20–28 km from central Bangkok.

faq.q: How much does Humz Canal Stay cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. ฿2,300/night for a Canal Deluxe Room · There are only 4 rooms in total — 1 Canal Suite (the largest) and 3 Canal Deluxe — and every room has a timber canal-view terrace · Prices rise and rooms sell out fast on long weekends and in high season because there are so few, so book well ahead and compare a few platforms first.

faq.q: Who is Humz Canal Stay best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples or anyone wanting to escape the city's bustle and relax quietly by a canal, who love a riverside atmosphere, good photos and sleeping to the sound of water · It accepts adults aged 18 and over only, with no extra beds, so it isn't suited to families with young children · If you want a soft bed, full facilities, or you're mainly here to see Bangkok, a hotel in the city or by the MRT will suit you better.

faq.q: What activities and facilities does Humz Canal Stay have?
faq.a: There's a riverside café called The Canal Club on site, kayaks for exploring the Om Non Canal, and a water-view terrace in every room · Breakfast is served pinto-style (Thai tiffin), and there's free Wi-Fi and parking; rooms have air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and an en-suite bathroom · Note that it's a small stay with no swimming pool, gym or hotel-style lobby, and some items aren't fully provided — bring your own essentials.

faq.q: What are the beds and sleeping like at Humz Canal Stay?
faq.a: Reviews consistently note fairly thin, firm mattresses — some describe them as around 10 cm thick — so anyone who likes a soft bed may need to adjust · There can also be some boat or community noise at night, so light sleepers should pack a favourite pillow or earplugs · Even so, many say waking to the canal view and sunrise from the terrace is well worth these limitations.

faq.q: What's the review score for Humz Canal Stay — can I trust it?
faq.a: Humz Canal Stay is a small canal-side stay of just 4 rooms, renovated from a 70-year-old wooden house, with a score around 9.0 from roughly 48 real guest reviews, which is high for a small, atmosphere-led place · Guests consistently praise the canal view, the quiet, the hosts' care and the pinto-style breakfast · It's a choice for travellers chasing a riverside experience rather than full convenience.
